description.narrative: Oxfam, in partnership with ESDC, proposes to reach 4,560 crisis-affected individuals (800 households) disaggregated as 1,115 Women,1,127 Men, 1,135 Girls, and 1,183 Boys in Gaza and North Gaza governorates in response to the acute humanitarian crisis resulting from the war and mass displacement. The target population consists of internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees and host community members who have been severely impacted by war, with a specific focus on vulnerable groups including women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities. The project will deliver an integrated, multi-sectoral response combining food security and protection interventions, ensuring that the same beneficiaries receive complementary assistance addressing both their immediate survival needs and critical protection concerns. The intervention will operate across two primary sectors: food security through voucher assistance and protection services encompassing psychosocial support, explosive ordnance risk education, and material assistance. Through the food security component, 800 vulnerable households will receive two rounds of restricted “to food” value vouchers, with dignified choice to meet their basic food needs while directly stimulating the recovering local market economy. Under the protection component, 1,200 individuals will receive explosive ordnance risk education to enhance community safety; 800 women and adolescent girls will access Psychological First Aid; 400 women and adolescent girls will receive individual counselling sessions; and 400women and girls will be provided with protection kits procured locally. The most important impact of this project will be the immediate improvement in food security for 800 vulnerable households through dignified voucher assistance while simultaneously strengthening their protection and psychosocial wellbeing through integrated case management, connecting at-risk families to essential services, reducing negative coping mechanisms, and fostering community resilience.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
